entries.title: Meandering River Cutting a Valley
entries.description: A flowing blue river ribbon curves across a slightly sloped green terrain mesh, with moving water particles eroding and carrying away brown terrain voxels, depositing lighter sand downstream and gradually widening bends over time.
entries.seed: Meandering River Cutting a Valley: A flowing blue river ribbon curves across a slightly sloped green terrain mesh, with moving water particles eroding and carrying away brown terrain voxels, depositing lighter sand downstream and gradually widening bends over time.

entries.title: Raindrop-Induced Hillslope Erosion
entries.description: Transparent raindrop spheres fall from a light sky onto a sloped, layered hillside block, loosening colored soil particles that detach, slide, and merge into tiny rivulets that carve branching channels down to a main river at the base.
entries.seed: Raindrop-Induced Hillslope Erosion: Transparent raindrop spheres fall from a light sky onto a sloped, layered hillside block, loosening colored soil particles that detach, slide, and merge into tiny rivulets that carve branching channels down to a main river at the base.

entries.title: Riverbank Undercutting and Collapse
entries.description: A main river channel flows beside tall, stratified riverbanks made of stacked colored layers; water particles collide with the bank, gradually dissolving support until chunks detach, tumble into the river, and are transported as rolling, bouncing blocks downstream.
entries.seed: Riverbank Undercutting and Collapse: A main river channel flows beside tall, stratified riverbanks made of stacked colored layers; water particles collide with the bank, gradually dissolving support until chunks detach, tumble into the river, and are transported as rolling, bouncing blocks downstream.

entries.title: Sediment Transport and Deposition Bars
entries.description: A straight river section carries colored sediment spheres of different sizes (gravels, sands, silts) that bounce and roll along the bed, settle into mid-channel sandbars and point bars, and are reshaped as flow speed (indicated by arrows and a meter) increases or decreases.

entries.title: Delta Formation at a Lake Mouth
entries.description: A river enters a calm, wide, transparent lake where suspended particles slow, settle, and build a branching delta structure; new distributary channels split and migrate across the growing delta, with labels tracking sediment thickness and shoreline position.

entries.title: Waterfall Retreat and Plunge Pool Erosion
entries.description: A river flows over a resistant rock ledge into a deep pool, where fast-moving water and swirling particle tracers scour the plunge pool and undercut the ledge, causing rock blocks to detach from the cliff face, fall, splash, and gradually move the waterfall upstream.

entries.title: Braided River Channel Dynamics
entries.description: A gently sloped valley floor hosts several shallow, shifting river threads that split and merge around transient sandbars; bars grow, shrink, and migrate as sediment is transferred, with trails marking past channel paths over a light background.

entries.title: Flood Event and Overbank Erosion
entries.description: A river cross-section with levees and a floodplain fills as water level rises; during a flood, water overtops banks, erodes levees, carves new overflow paths, and deposits a thin, colored silt layer across the floodplain, with a time-lapse slider to replay the event.

entries.title: Bedrock River Incision Through Uplifted Terrain
entries.description: A river cuts down through a rising block of layered rock; as the base level drops, the river bed incises, forming a canyon with steep walls, knickpoints that migrate upstream, and labeled terraces marking former river levels.

entries.title: Sediment Sorting Along a River Profile
entries.description: A long, gently curving 3D river profile shows large, medium, and small sediment spheres moving from steep headwaters to flat lowlands, with larger particles dropping out earlier and smaller ones traveling farther, color-coding where each size class accumulates.

entries.title: Oxbow Lake Formation from Meander Cutoff
entries.description: A sinuous river gradually exaggerates its meanders as bank erosion shifts the channel, until two nearby limbs collide and merge, cutting off a loop that becomes a still, semi-transparent oxbow lake while the main channel straightens and abandons the old path.

entries.title: Ice-Dammed River and Catastrophic Outburst
entries.description: A river is blocked by a translucent ice dam, forming a growing lake upstream; as water pressure builds, cracks glow and widen in the ice until the dam fails, releasing a surge that erodes the downstream channel, strips banks, and deposits a thick sediment wedge.

entries.title: Tidal River Mouth and Estuary Erosion
entries.description: A river meets the ocean in an estuary where rising and falling water levels (animated surface plane) reverse flow direction; tidal currents alternately erode and deposit sediments in the channel and on tidal flats, reshaping sandbars and channel depth.

entries.title: Cross-Sectional Channel Shape Adjustment
entries.description: A 3D slice of a river cross-section shows water shear stress along the bed and banks; faster zones erode, widening and deepening the channel, while slower inner zones accumulate sediment, changing the cross-section from narrow/deep to wide/shallow or vice versa.

entries.description: A plan-view river channel with evenly spaced bank markers shows successive positions of the banks as the river migrates laterally, eroding outer bends and depositing on inner bends, leaving behind color-coded “ghost” outlines of former channel positions.

entries.description: A cold-region river cuts into frozen, ice-rich banks; as warmer water and air melt ground ice, sections slump as large rotating blocks, slide into the channel, and melt into muddy flows that mix with the river and increase sediment load.
